title: End-to-End Project Leadership and Value Delivery Capstone
summary: Integrate people leadership, delivery tailoring, governance, risk/change control and business-value reasoning into a complex project scenario.
scenario: Lead a strategically important project with stakeholder conflict, delivery uncertainty, regulatory constraints and changing benefit assumptions.
functional_requirements: Tailor the delivery approach to uncertainty and governance context.
Resolve stakeholder and team conflict without bypassing accountability.
Integrate risk, issue, quality and change evidence.
Protect benefits and strategic alignment when scope pressure increases.
Produce an evidence-backed decision log and executive recommendation.
validation: Passes when the learner can defend context-sensitive decisions that protect people, governance, value and delivery outcomes.

assessment_rubric.governance: Uses risk/change mechanisms without bureaucracy theatre.
assessment_rubric.value: Connects decisions to outcomes, benefits and business impact.

title: Strategic PMO Operating Model and Portfolio Governance Capstone
summary: Integrate PMO mandate, service portfolio, governance, assurance and measurable value into an enterprise PMO redesign exercise.
scenario: Redesign a PMO viewed as bureaucratic while the organization suffers weak prioritization, poor benefits visibility and inconsistent decision data.
functional_requirements: Reconfirm mandate, sponsor, customers and decision rights.
Redesign the PMO service portfolio around demonstrated needs.
Define portfolio prioritization and assurance evidence.
Replace activity metrics with value and decision-quality measures.
Create a phased operating-model improvement plan with executive governance boundaries.
validation: Passes when the learner can show how the PMO improves decisions, strategic alignment, benefits and delivery capability without adding low-value control.

assessment_rubric.mandate: Aligns PMO purpose to context and customers.
assessment_rubric.value: Uses outcome/value metrics rather than activity volume.
assessment_rubric.adaptability: Retires or redesigns low-value PMO services.

title: Professional Scrum Team Effectiveness Capstone
summary: Integrate empiricism, accountabilities, goals, artifacts, flow, quality and coaching into a Scrum-team improvement exercise.
scenario: Coach a Scrum Team that completes substantial work but has weak goals, recurring carry-over, quality debt and low stakeholder value.
functional_requirements: Assess Product Goal, Sprint Goal and Definition of Done quality.
Identify accountability and self-management anti-patterns.
Diagnose flow, feedback and stakeholder-engagement weaknesses.
Propose coaching experiments without command-and-control intervention.
Define evidence that would show improved value, quality and empiricism.
validation: Passes when the learner can improve Scrum outcomes without reducing Scrum to ceremony compliance or velocity targets.

assessment_rubric.empiricism: Uses transparency, inspection and adaptation correctly.
assessment_rubric.quality: Protects Definition of Done and usable increments.
assessment_rubric.coaching: Uses evidence-based coaching instead of directive task management.

title: Adaptive Delivery, Flow and Enterprise Agility Capstone
summary: Integrate agile mindset, lifecycle selection, flow, feedback, product thinking and modern metrics into an enterprise delivery redesign.
scenario: Redesign a delivery system with overloaded WIP, slow feedback, output-driven metrics and mixed predictive/agile dependencies.
functional_requirements: Choose fit-for-purpose iterative, flow or hybrid delivery patterns.
Map queues, handoffs, blocked work and feedback latency.
Define outcome and flow measures that resist gaming.
Preserve governance proportional to risk and compliance.
Design improvement experiments with measurable business/customer outcomes.
validation: Passes when the learner can improve end-to-end value flow without equating Agile with one framework or eliminating necessary governance.

assessment_rubric.mindset: Applies agile values and principles contextually.
assessment_rubric.flow: Uses WIP/lead-time evidence to improve system behavior.
assessment_rubric.measurement: Prefers outcome and learning metrics over vanity output metrics.
assessment_rubric.governance: Balances adaptability with risk and compliance needs.

title: Digital Service Value, Operations and Continual Improvement Capstone
summary: Integrate ITIL value-system thinking, operational practices, service levels, experience, governance and continual improvement into a service-recovery and improvement exercise.
scenario: Recover and improve a business-critical digital service with recurring incidents, poor user experience, weak problem follow-up and disputed service-level outcomes.
functional_requirements: Separate incident restoration from problem analysis and continual improvement.
Use change enablement without bypassing incident authority.
Connect technical health to service level and user experience.
Map suppliers, dependencies and value-stream constraints.
Define measurable continual-improvement actions and verification.
validation: Passes when the learner can restore, govern and improve service value without optimizing isolated process metrics.

assessment_rubric.value: Connects practices to outcomes and experience.
assessment_rubric.operations: Separates incident, problem and change objectives correctly.
assessment_rubric.governance: Preserves authority and risk control during urgent work.
assessment_rubric.improvement: Defines measurable, owned improvement with outcome verification.
